title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2611.30190v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Success-rate gains guide the development of web agents. Yet knowing which agent ranks first does not tell us how much confidence to place in its reported advantage. We study the comparison itself: how success is defined, what evidence supports the judgments, and how the difference between agents is estimated. On fixed web-agent executions, changing a judge from predicting likely completion to requiring recorded support can remove most of a reported lead without changing the ranking. This effect persists when unresolved completion is distinguished from supported failure. Controlled source additions explain how missing relations between task requirements, objects and observations can conceal a difference or create an apparent advantage. We also find that making both agents' score estimates more accurate can make their difference less accurate, because their original errors partly canceled. translated_title: 相同执行、不同差距：Web智能体评估中的判定规则
translated_abstract: 成功率的提升引导着Web智能体的发展。然而，知道哪个智能体排名第一并不能告诉我们应该对其所报告的优势抱有多大的信心。我们研究的是比较过程本身：成功是如何定义的、什么样的证据支持这些判断，以及智能体之间的差异是如何被估计的。在固定的Web智能体执行记录上，将评判者从预测可能完成任务改为要求有记录的证据支持，可以在不改变排名的情况下消除大部分所报告的领先优势。当把未确定的完成与有证据支持的失败区分开时，这种效应依然存在。通过受控的证据来源添加实验，我们解释了任务需求、对象和观察之间缺失的关联如何掩盖真实差异或制造出表面上的优势。我们还发现，让两个智能体的分数估计都更加准确，反而可能使它们之间差异的估计更不准确，因为它们最初的误差部分地相互抵消了。为了估计所选定的结果差异，我们结合……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了Web智能体评估中的判定规则问题：评判标准与证据要求的选择可以在不改变排名的情况下大幅改变所报告的性能差距，且提高双方分数估计的准确性反而可能降低差异估计的准确性。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that judgment rules in web-agent evaluation—how success is defined and what evidence is required—can eliminate most of a reported performance lead without changing rankings, and that making both agents' score estimates more accurate can paradoxically make the difference between them less accurate.
